title: A Neural Tangent Kernel Perspective of Infinite Tree Ensembles

en.text: On tabular data, gradient-boosted and neural decision trees remain the models to beat. One increasingly popular variant is the soft tree ensemble: instead of the hard, greedy splits of a classic decision tree, every splitting rule is made differentiable, so the whole forest can be trained end-to-end with gradient descent, exactly like a neural network. These models perform well, and practitioners have accumulated a toolbox of tricks to train them: sharing parameters across nodes, tuning how sharp the splits are, over-parameterizing the ensemble. What has been missing is theory. Almost nothing explained why soft tree ensembles train the way they do, when they generalize, or why those tricks work.

For neural networks, the tool that filled a similar gap was the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK). In the limit of infinitely many hidden units, a wide network trained by gradient descent behaves like kernel regression with a fixed, closed-form kernel, and that observation has explained training dynamics and generalization for the MLP, the CNN, and many other architectures. Each architecture induces its own distinct kernel. But no one had derived an NTK for tree models, so the soft-tree side of the tabular world stayed theoretically dark.

This paper, presented at ICLR 2022 by Ryuichi Kanoh and Mahito Sugiyama (National Institute of Informatics, NII, and SOKENDAI), closes that gap. It introduces the Tree Neural Tangent Kernel (TNTK): the kernel induced by an ensemble of infinitely many soft trees. From a single closed-form kernel, the authors derive global training convergence, prove that the parameter sharing used by oblivious-tree models costs nothing in this limit, show why very deep soft trees stop generalizing, and explain why sharper splits produce a more useful kernel.

en.caption: Figure 1. An ensemble of M soft trees. Each perfect binary tree routes an input through differentiable internal nodes (blue, with weight vectors w) down to leaf values (green, the response π). Every tree outputs a weighted sum over its leaves, and the ensemble averages the M tree outputs with a 1/√M scaling. The TNTK studies the limit M → ∞.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04983
From soft trees to a fixed kernel

A soft tree replaces each hard split with a smooth decision. At every internal node, instead of sending an input strictly left or right, the tree computes a probability of going each way using a scaled error function — essentially a smooth sigmoid whose steepness is set by a scaling parameter α. Small α gives a gentle, almost linear split; as α grows the split sharpens, and in the limit α → ∞ it recovers the hard split of an ordinary decision tree. Because every operation is differentiable, the internal weights and the leaf values can all be learned jointly by gradient descent.

The authors take an ensemble of M perfect binary soft trees of depth d, initialize the parameters randomly, and let M go to infinity. Their central result is that the ensemble's neural tangent kernel converges in probability to a deterministic kernel that no longer depends on the random initialization. The TNTK has a clean, interpretable structure: one contribution from the internal splitting nodes and one from the leaves, combined in closed form. Crucially, the split expectations have analytic expressions, so the whole kernel is available as a formula rather than a simulation. And because that formula is not a depth-by-depth recursion, computing the TNTK costs the same no matter how deep the trees are — a point that will matter later.

The formula folds together two ingredients evaluated on a pair of inputs: T, the probability that both inputs are routed the same way at a node, and its derivative in the input similarity. Written compactly, the depth-d kernel is 2^d · d · Σ · T^(d-1) · Ṫ  +  (2T)^d, where Σ is the inner product of the two inputs. The first term is the internal-node contribution, the second the leaf contribution; both are fixed once α and d are chosen.
Why training is guaranteed to converge

The reason a fixed kernel is such a useful object is that it turns a hard question about gradient descent into an easy one about linear algebra. The authors show that during training the TNTK stays essentially constant, so learning an infinite soft-tree ensemble reduces to kernel regression with the TNTK. Because the kernel is positive definite, that regression has a unique solution and gradient descent converges to it globally — there is no getting stuck in a bad local minimum. Before trusting this limit, though, it is worth checking that a finite ensemble actually approaches it.

en.caption: Figure 2. The finite-ensemble kernel approaches the closed-form TNTK. Left: for two inputs whose angle is swept, the empirical kernel (colored) tightens onto the analytic limit (dotted black) as the number of trees M grows from 16 to 4096. Center and right: the relative error between the empirical and limiting kernels falls at the expected M^(-1/2) rate across split-hardness α and depth d.

en.text: The convergence is not just asymptotic hand-waving. As the ensemble grows, the empirical kernel tightens onto the analytic TNTK at the M^(-1/2) rate the theory predicts, and it does so consistently as the split hardness α and the tree depth d are varied. With the limiting kernel validated, the kernel-regression picture of training can be tested directly.

en.caption: Figure 3. Training dynamics match the kernel-regression prediction. Each color is one train (left) or test (right) point; the thick analytical curve is the trajectory the limiting TNTK predicts, and the dashed lines are actual soft-tree ensembles (M = 1024) trained by gradient descent. Even a modest ensemble (M = 16, dotted) tracks the prediction, and M = 1024 follows it closely.

en.text: When the authors train real soft-tree ensembles and overlay the output trajectory the TNTK predicts, the two agree — closely for M = 1024, and recognizably even for M = 16. The infinite-width theory is describing the behavior of finite, trainable models, not just an idealized limit.
Oblivious trees come for free

A popular design choice in models like NODE is the oblivious tree: within a given depth, all internal nodes share the same splitting rule, which drastically cuts the number of parameters and makes the tree easy to vectorize. It is natural to worry that this constraint sacrifices expressive power. The TNTK gives a clean answer.

en.caption: Figure 4. Normal tree (left) versus oblivious tree (right). In the oblivious tree, the splitting rule is shared across all nodes at the same depth (the boxed w-vectors are identical), while the leaf responses π can still differ. The paper proves both induce the same TNTK in the infinite limit.

en.text: The authors prove that an ensemble of oblivious soft trees converges to exactly the same TNTK as an ensemble of ordinary soft trees. In the infinite limit, sharing splitting rules within a depth costs nothing in kernel terms — the very architectural constraint that makes oblivious trees efficient turns out to be free. That is a reassuring theoretical footing for a design many practitioners already use.
Sharper splits help; deeper trees degenerate

Because the TNTK is available in closed form, one can simply plot it and read off how the two knobs — split hardness α and depth d — reshape the kernel. This is where the theory starts to explain empirical folklore.

en.caption: Figure 5. How α and depth shape the kernel, as a function of the inner product between two inputs. Left three panels (colored by α): as splits sharpen, the kernel bends away from a straight line into a more expressive, nonlinear shape. Right panel (colored by depth d): as trees get deeper, the kernel flattens toward zero everywhere except at perfect similarity — the degeneracy that predicts poor generalization.

en.text: Two readings come straight off these curves. First, when α is small the kernel is nearly linear, so the model can barely express nonlinear structure; as α grows the kernel bends into a richer shape. This matches the intuition that a near-linear soft split is too gentle to be useful. Second, and less obviously, as depth increases the kernel degenerates: it collapses toward a constant, responding only when two inputs are almost identical. A kernel that treats nearly all pairs of inputs as equally dissimilar cannot generalize well, which is the paper's explanation for why very deep soft trees underperform.
Does it work? Kernel regression on 90 datasets

Theory in hand, the authors test the TNTK as a practical kernel. They run kernel regression with the TNTK on 90 real-world datasets, tuning depth from d = 1 to 29, and compare against the kernel induced by an infinitely wide MLP and against the classic RBF kernel.

en.caption: Figure 6. Left: averaged accuracy over 90 datasets versus tree depth, for a range of split-hardness values α, with the MLP-induced NTK and RBF baselines shown for reference. Accuracy first rises then falls with depth — exactly the degeneracy the kernel shape predicts. Right: kernel-computation time versus depth. The TNTK (orange) stays flat while the MLP-induced NTK (blue) grows linearly with depth.

en.text: The depth sweep reproduces the predicted degeneracy directly: averaged accuracy climbs for the first few levels and then declines as trees get deeper, for every setting of α. The timing panel makes the closed-form payoff concrete — because the TNTK does not recurse in depth, its cost is essentially flat, whereas the MLP-induced NTK grows linearly with depth. On the accuracy comparison, the MLP-induced kernel is stronger on average, but the tree kernel is not merely a curiosity: it wins outright on more than 30% of the individual datasets, exactly the cases where a tree's inductive bias is the better fit.

The split-hardness sweep quantifies the "sharper is better" story. The table below reports, for each α, the fraction of the 90 datasets on which the TNTK beats the MLP-induced NTK. The win rate climbs from 13.6% at the near-linear α = 0.5 to a peak of 34.9% at α = 32, and the whole hard-split range sits comfortably above the 11.8% managed by the RBF kernel.

en.caption: Table 1. TNTK win rate against the MLP-induced NTK across the 90 datasets, as a function of split hardness α (depth tuned from d = 1 to 29). The RBF kernel is shown for reference.

en.text: Takeaways

The lasting contribution is conceptual: the NTK framework, previously a tool for neural networks, extends cleanly to tree ensembles. The resulting Tree NTK explains a range of soft-tree behavior from one theory — training converges globally, oblivious parameter sharing is free in the infinite limit, deep trees degenerate into a near-constant kernel, and sharper splits yield a more expressive one. Along the way it delivers a usable, depth-free kernel that is competitive with, and on more than 30% of datasets better than, the MLP-induced NTK, at a fraction of the computational cost as depth grows.

The honest boundaries are worth stating. The analysis lives in the infinite-ensemble limit and covers perfect binary trees; the empirical study is kernel regression on tabular datasets rather than large-scale deep learning, and on average the MLP-induced kernel still edges out the tree kernel. Even so, the TNTK gives soft tree ensembles something they lacked — a principled account of why they train and generalize as they do, and a concrete guide to the tricks that make them work.

zh.text: 在表格数据（tabular data）上，基于决策树的模型至今仍是最难被超越的一类。近年来一个受关注的变体是「软树集成（soft tree ensemble）」：它不像经典决策树那样在每个节点做硬性贪心划分，而是把每条分裂规则都改造成可微分形式，于是整片森林可以像神经网络一样用梯度下降端到端训练。这类模型在许多任务上表现很好，实践者也积累了一套训练技巧：节点间共享参数、调节分裂软硬、把集成过参数化。唯一缺的是理论——几乎没有工作能解释它们为何这样训练、何时能泛化，以及这些经验技巧为何有效。
对神经网络来说，填补类似空白的工具正是「神经正切核（Neural Tangent Kernel, NTK）」。在隐藏单元数趋于无穷的极限下，用梯度下降训练的宽网络等价于一个固定、有闭式表达的核所对应的核回归；这一观察解释了 MLP、CNN 等众多架构的训练动力学与泛化，而每种架构都会诱导出属于自己的核。但此前没有人为树模型推导出对应的 NTK，于是表格世界里软树这一侧一直处在理论的暗处。

这篇发表于 ICLR 2022 的论文，由日本国立情报学研究所（NII）与综合研究大学院大学（SOKENDAI）的 Ryuichi Kanoh 和 Mahito Sugiyama 完成，补上了这块拼图。他们提出「树的神经正切核（Tree Neural Tangent Kernel, TNTK）」，即由无穷多棵软树组成的集成所诱导的核。从这一个闭式核出发，作者推导出训练的全局收敛，证明 oblivious 树的参数共享在该极限下不损失表达力，并解释了深软树为何反而不再泛化、以及把分裂做硬为何更有用。

zh.caption: 图 1 由 M 棵软树组成的集成。每棵完全二叉树把输入沿可微分的内部节点（蓝色，带权向量 w）向下路由，直到叶子取值（绿色，即响应 π）。每棵树输出叶子上的加权和，集成再把 M 棵树的输出以 1/√M 的比例平均。TNTK 研究的是 M → ∞ 的极限。

zh.text: 论文链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04983
从软树到一个固定的核

软树把每个硬分裂替换成一次平滑的决策。在每个内部节点上，输入不再被严格地分到左边或右边，而是用一个「缩放误差函数（scaled error function）」计算向两侧走的概率——本质上是一个平滑的 sigmoid，其陡峭程度由缩放参数 α 控制。α 较小时分裂很温和、接近线性；α 增大时分裂变硬，而在 α → ∞ 的极限下就还原成普通决策树的硬分裂。由于每一步操作都可微分，内部权重和叶子取值都能用梯度下降联合学习。

作者取 M 棵深度为 d 的完全二叉软树组成集成，随机初始化参数，再让 M 趋于无穷。他们的核心结论是：该集成的神经正切核会依概率收敛到一个确定性的核，不再依赖随机初始化。TNTK 有一个清晰、可解释的结构：一部分来自内部分裂节点，一部分来自叶子，二者以闭式组合。关键在于，分裂的期望有解析表达式，所以整个核是一个公式而非一次模拟。又因为这个公式并不是对深度逐层递归的，计算 TNTK 的开销与树有多深无关——这一点在后面很重要。
这个公式把在一对输入上求值的两个量组合在一起：T，即两个输入在某节点被路由到同一侧的概率，以及它对输入相似度的导数。写得紧凑一些，深度为 d 的核是 2^d · d · Σ · T^(d-1) · Ṫ  +  (2T)^d，其中 Σ 是两个输入的内积。第一项是内部节点的贡献，第二项是叶子的贡献；一旦选定 α 与 d，二者都被固定下来。
为什么训练一定会收敛
固定的核之所以是个如此有用的对象，是因为它把一个关于梯度下降的难题，转化成一个关于线性代数的简单问题。作者证明，训练过程中 TNTK 基本保持不变，于是训练一个无穷软树集成就退化为用 TNTK 做核回归。由于该核是正定的，这个回归有唯一解，梯度下降会全局收敛到它——不会卡在糟糕的局部极小值里。不过在信任这个极限之前，值得先确认有限规模的集成确实在向它靠近。

zh.caption: 图 2 有限集成的核向闭式 TNTK 收敛。左：对夹角被逐步扫过的两个输入，经验核（彩色）随着树的数量 M 从 16 增到 4096，逐渐贴合到解析极限（黑色虚线）。中与右：经验核与极限核之间的相对误差，在不同分裂硬度 α 与深度 d 下都按理论预期的 M^(-1/2) 速率下降。

zh.text: 这种收敛并不是空泛的渐近说辞。随着集成变大，经验核以理论预测的 M^(-1/2) 速率贴合解析 TNTK，并且在改变分裂硬度 α 和树深度 d 时都保持一致。极限核得到验证之后，就可以直接检验训练的核回归图景了。

zh.caption: 图 3 训练动力学与核回归的预测吻合。每种颜色是一个训练点（左）或测试点（右）；粗的解析曲线是极限 TNTK 预测的轨迹，虚线是用梯度下降真实训练的软树集成（M = 1024）。即便是较小的集成（M = 16，点线）也能跟上预测，而 M = 1024 几乎与之重合。

zh.text: 当作者真正训练软树集成，并把 TNTK 预测的输出轨迹叠加上去时，两者吻合——M = 1024 时贴合紧密，M = 16 时也能辨认出同样的走势。这说明无穷宽度的理论描述的是有限、可训练模型的行为，而不只是一个理想化的极限。
Oblivious 树是「免费」的
在 NODE 等模型里有一个流行的设计选择：oblivious 树——在同一深度上，所有内部节点共享同一条分裂规则，这大幅减少了参数量，也让树容易向量化。人们自然会担心，这种约束是否牺牲了表达能力。TNTK 给出了一个干净的答案。

zh.caption: 图 4 普通树（左）与 oblivious 树（右）。在 oblivious 树中，同一深度上的分裂规则被共享（框内的 w 向量彼此相同），而叶子响应 π 仍可不同。论文证明，二者在无穷极限下诱导出完全相同的 TNTK。

zh.text: 作者证明，oblivious 软树集成会收敛到与普通软树集成完全相同的 TNTK。在无穷极限下，在同一深度共享分裂规则在核的意义上不付出任何代价——正是那个让 oblivious 树高效的架构约束，结果是免费的。这为许多实践者早已在用的设计，提供了一个令人安心的理论依据。
分裂更硬更好，树更深却退化
因为 TNTK 有闭式表达，我们可以直接把它画出来，读出两个旋钮——分裂硬度 α 与深度 d——如何重塑这个核。理论也正是从这里开始解释那些经验性的「老规矩」。

zh.caption: 图 5 α 与深度如何塑造核，横轴是两个输入的内积。左侧三幅（按 α 上色）：分裂越硬，核越偏离直线，弯成更有表达力的非线性形状。右侧一幅（按深度 d 上色）：树越深，核在几乎所有相似度上都被压平到零，只在完全相似处才有响应——这就是预示泛化变差的退化现象。

zh.text: 从这些曲线可以直接读出两点。第一，当 α 很小时核几乎是线性的，模型几乎无法表达非线性结构；α 增大后核弯成更丰富的形状。这与「太温和的近线性软分裂没什么用」的直觉一致。第二，也更不易察觉：随着深度增加，核会退化，坍缩成一个近乎常数、只在两个输入几乎完全相同时才有反应的核。一个把几乎所有输入对都视作同样不相似的核，是无法很好泛化的——这正是论文对「很深的软树表现变差」的解释。
到底管不管用？90 个数据集上的核回归
有了理论，作者把 TNTK 当作一个实用的核来检验。他们在 90 个真实世界数据集上用 TNTK 做核回归，把深度从 d = 1 调到 29，并与无穷宽 MLP 诱导的核以及经典的 RBF 核作对比。

zh.caption: 图 6 左：90 个数据集上的平均准确率随树深度的变化（多条曲线对应不同分裂硬度 α），并以 MLP 诱导的 NTK 与 RBF 作参照；准确率随深度先升后降，正是核形状所预测的退化。右：核计算耗时，TNTK（橙）基本平坦，MLP 诱导 NTK（蓝）随深度线性增长。

zh.text: 深度扫描直接复现了预测的退化：对每一个 α，平均准确率都在最初几层上升，随后随着树变深而下降。耗时那一幅则把闭式的好处落到实处——由于 TNTK 不对深度递归，它的开销基本是平的，而 MLP 诱导的 NTK 则随深度线性增长。在准确率对比上，MLP 诱导的核平均更强，但树的核并不只是个摆设：它在超过 30% 的单个数据集上取胜，也就是那些树的归纳偏置更契合数据的场景。
分裂硬度的扫描量化了「越硬越好」这个故事。下表给出在每个 α 下，TNTK 在 90 个数据集中胜过 MLP 诱导 NTK 的比例。胜率从近线性的 α = 0.5 时的 13.6% 一路爬升，到 α = 32 时达到峰值 34.9%，而整个硬分裂区间都明显高于 RBF 核的 11.8%。

zh.caption: 表 1 在 90 个数据集上，TNTK 相对 MLP 诱导 NTK 的胜率，随分裂硬度 α 变化（深度从 d = 1 到 29 调优）。RBF 核作为参照。

zh.text: 小结

这篇工作最持久的贡献是观念上的：原本只用于神经网络的 NTK 框架，可以干净地推广到树集成上。由此得到的 Tree NTK 用一套理论解释了软树的一系列行为——训练全局收敛、oblivious 参数共享在无穷极限下免费、深树退化成近乎常数的核、分裂更硬则核更有表达力。它同时给出一个实用、与深度无关的核：与 MLP 诱导的 NTK 有竞争力，在超过 30% 的数据集上更优，且随深度增长计算成本远低于后者。
边界也值得说明。分析建立在无穷集成极限之上，且针对完全二叉树；实证是表格数据上的核回归而非大规模深度学习，平均而言 MLP 诱导的核仍略胜一筹。即便如此，TNTK 给了软树集成此前缺少的东西——一个关于它们为何这样训练、这样泛化的原理性解释。

en.title: ICLR 2022: A Neural Tangent Kernel for Infinite Tree Ensembles
en.subtitle: Kanoh and Sugiyama derive the Tree NTK, the first kernel-theoretic account of soft decision-tree ensembles, and use it to explain why parameter sharing is free, why deep trees degenerate, and why harder splits help.

zh.text: 为什么训练一定会收敛
固定的核之所以是个如此有用的对象，是因为它把一个关于梯度下降的难题，转化成一个关于线性代数的简单问题。作者证明，训练过程中 TNTK 基本保持不变，于是训练一个无穷软树集成就退化为用 TNTK 做核回归。由于该核是正定的，这个回归有唯一解，梯度下降会全局收敛到它——不会卡在糟糕的局部极小值里。不过在信任这个极限之前，值得先确认有限规模的集成确实在向它靠近。

zh.caption: 图 2 有限集成的核向闭式 TNTK 收敛。左：对夹角被逐步扫过的两个输入，经验核（彩色）随着树的数量 M 从 16 增到 4096，逐渐贴合到解析极限（黑色虚线）。中与右：经验核与极限核之间的相对误差，在不同分裂硬度 α 与深度 d 下都按理论预期的 M^(-1/2) 速率下降。

zh.text: 这种收敛并不是空泛的渐近说辞。随着集成变大，经验核以理论预测的 M^(-1/2) 速率贴合解析 TNTK，并且在改变分裂硬度 α 和树深度 d 时都保持一致。极限核得到验证之后，就可以直接检验训练的核回归图景了。

zh.caption: 图 3 训练动力学与核回归的预测吻合。每种颜色是一个训练点（左）或测试点（右）；粗的解析曲线是极限 TNTK 预测的轨迹，虚线是用梯度下降真实训练的软树集成（M = 1024）。即便是较小的集成（M = 16，点线）也能跟上预测，而 M = 1024 几乎与之重合。

zh.text: 当作者真正训练软树集成，并把 TNTK 预测的输出轨迹叠加上去时，两者吻合——M = 1024 时贴合紧密，M = 16 时也能辨认出同样的走势。这说明无穷宽度的理论描述的是有限、可训练模型的行为，而不只是一个理想化的极限。

en.title: ICLR 2022: A Neural Tangent Kernel for Infinite Tree Ensembles
en.subtitle: Kanoh and Sugiyama derive the Tree NTK, the first kernel-theoretic account of soft decision-tree ensembles, and use it to explain why parameter sharing is free, why deep trees degenerate, and why harder splits help.

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 给无穷棵软树一把「核」尺子：Tree NTK 首次为软树集成提供理论解释
zh.subtitle: 日本国立情报学研究所 Kanoh 与 Sugiyama 推导出树的神经正切核（TNTK），一套理论同时解释了软树集成的全局收敛、参数共享为何免费、深树为何退化、以及分裂更硬为何更好。

en.caption: Figure 1. An ensemble of M soft trees. Each perfect binary tree routes an input through differentiable internal nodes (blue, with weight vectors w) down to leaf values (green, the response π). Every tree outputs a weighted sum over its leaves, and the ensemble averages the M tree outputs with a 1/√M scaling. The TNTK studies the limit M → ∞.

en.text: From soft trees to a fixed kernel

A soft tree replaces each hard split with a smooth decision. At every internal node, instead of sending an input strictly left or right, the tree computes a probability of going each way using a scaled error function — essentially a smooth sigmoid whose steepness is set by a scaling parameter α. Small α gives a gentle, almost linear split; as α grows the split sharpens, and in the limit α → ∞ it recovers the hard split of an ordinary decision tree. Because every operation is differentiable, the internal weights and the leaf values can all be learned jointly by gradient descent.

The authors take an ensemble of M perfect binary soft trees of depth d, initialize the parameters randomly, and let M go to infinity. Their central result is that the ensemble's neural tangent kernel converges in probability to a deterministic kernel that no longer depends on the random initialization. The TNTK has a clean, interpretable structure: one contribution from the internal splitting nodes and one from the leaves, combined in closed form. Crucially, the split expectations have analytic expressions, so the whole kernel is available as a formula rather than a simulation. And because that formula is not a depth-by-depth recursion, computing the TNTK costs the same no matter how deep the trees are — a point that will matter later.

The formula folds together two ingredients evaluated on a pair of inputs: T, the probability that both inputs are routed the same way at a node, and its derivative in the input similarity. Written compactly, the depth-d kernel is 2^d · d · Σ · T^(d-1) · Ṫ  +  (2T)^d, where Σ is the inner product of the two inputs. The first term is the internal-node contribution, the second the leaf contribution; both are fixed once α and d are chosen.

zh.caption: 图 1 由 M 棵软树组成的集成。每棵完全二叉树把输入沿可微分的内部节点（蓝色，带权向量 w）向下路由，直到叶子取值（绿色，即响应 π）。每棵树输出叶子上的加权和，集成再把 M 棵树的输出以 1/√M 的比例平均。TNTK 研究的是 M → ∞ 的极限。

zh.text: 从软树到一个固定的核

软树把每个硬分裂替换成一次平滑的决策。在每个内部节点上，输入不再被严格地分到左边或右边，而是用一个「缩放误差函数（scaled error function）」计算向两侧走的概率——本质上是一个平滑的 sigmoid，其陡峭程度由缩放参数 α 控制。α 较小时分裂很温和、接近线性；α 增大时分裂变硬，而在 α → ∞ 的极限下就还原成普通决策树的硬分裂。由于每一步操作都可微分，内部权重和叶子取值都能用梯度下降联合学习。

作者取 M 棵深度为 d 的完全二叉软树组成集成，随机初始化参数，再让 M 趋于无穷。他们的核心结论是：该集成的神经正切核会依概率收敛到一个确定性的核，不再依赖随机初始化。TNTK 有一个清晰、可解释的结构：一部分来自内部分裂节点，一部分来自叶子，二者以闭式组合。关键在于，分裂的期望有解析表达式，所以整个核是一个公式而非一次模拟。又因为这个公式并不是对深度逐层递归的，计算 TNTK 的开销与树有多深无关——这一点在后面很重要。
这个公式把在一对输入上求值的两个量组合在一起：T，即两个输入在某节点被路由到同一侧的概率，以及它对输入相似度的导数。写得紧凑一些，深度为 d 的核是 2^d · d · Σ · T^(d-1) · Ṫ  +  (2T)^d，其中 Σ 是两个输入的内积。第一项是内部节点的贡献，第二项是叶子的贡献；一旦选定 α 与 d，二者都被固定下来。

en.subtitle: Kanoh and Sugiyama derive the Tree NTK, the first kernel-theoretic account of soft decision-tree ensembles, and use it to explain why parameter sharing is free, why deep trees degenerate, and why harder splits help.

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 给无穷棵软树一把「核」尺子：Tree NTK 首次为软树集成提供理论解释
zh.subtitle: 日本国立情报学研究所 Kanoh 与 Sugiyama 推导出树的神经正切核（TNTK），一套理论同时解释了软树集成的全局收敛、参数共享为何免费、深树为何退化、以及分裂更硬为何更好。

en.text: Oblivious trees come for free

A popular design choice in models like NODE is the oblivious tree: within a given depth, all internal nodes share the same splitting rule, which drastically cuts the number of parameters and makes the tree easy to vectorize. It is natural to worry that this constraint sacrifices expressive power. The TNTK gives a clean answer.

en.caption: Figure 4. Normal tree (left) versus oblivious tree (right). In the oblivious tree, the splitting rule is shared across all nodes at the same depth (the boxed w-vectors are identical), while the leaf responses π can still differ. The paper proves both induce the same TNTK in the infinite limit.

en.text: The authors prove that an ensemble of oblivious soft trees converges to exactly the same TNTK as an ensemble of ordinary soft trees. In the infinite limit, sharing splitting rules within a depth costs nothing in kernel terms — the very architectural constraint that makes oblivious trees efficient turns out to be free. That is a reassuring theoretical footing for a design many practitioners already use.

zh.text: Oblivious 树是「免费」的
在 NODE 等模型里有一个流行的设计选择：oblivious 树——在同一深度上，所有内部节点共享同一条分裂规则，这大幅减少了参数量，也让树容易向量化。人们自然会担心，这种约束是否牺牲了表达能力。TNTK 给出了一个干净的答案。

zh.caption: 图 4 普通树（左）与 oblivious 树（右）。在 oblivious 树中，同一深度上的分裂规则被共享（框内的 w 向量彼此相同），而叶子响应 π 仍可不同。论文证明，二者在无穷极限下诱导出完全相同的 TNTK。

zh.text: 作者证明，oblivious 软树集成会收敛到与普通软树集成完全相同的 TNTK。在无穷极限下，在同一深度共享分裂规则在核的意义上不付出任何代价——正是那个让 oblivious 树高效的架构约束，结果是免费的。这为许多实践者早已在用的设计，提供了一个令人安心的理论依据。

en.title: ICLR 2022: A Neural Tangent Kernel for Infinite Tree Ensembles
en.subtitle: Kanoh and Sugiyama derive the Tree NTK, the first kernel-theoretic account of soft decision-tree ensembles, and use it to explain why parameter sharing is free, why deep trees degenerate, and why harder splits help.

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 给无穷棵软树一把「核」尺子：Tree NTK 首次为软树集成提供理论解释
zh.subtitle: 日本国立情报学研究所 Kanoh 与 Sugiyama 推导出树的神经正切核（TNTK），一套理论同时解释了软树集成的全局收敛、参数共享为何免费、深树为何退化、以及分裂更硬为何更好。

en.text: Does it work? Kernel regression on 90 datasets

Theory in hand, the authors test the TNTK as a practical kernel. They run kernel regression with the TNTK on 90 real-world datasets, tuning depth from d = 1 to 29, and compare against the kernel induced by an infinitely wide MLP and against the classic RBF kernel.

en.caption: Figure 6. Left: averaged accuracy over 90 datasets versus tree depth, for a range of split-hardness values α, with the MLP-induced NTK and RBF baselines shown for reference. Accuracy first rises then falls with depth — exactly the degeneracy the kernel shape predicts. Right: kernel-computation time versus depth. The TNTK (orange) stays flat while the MLP-induced NTK (blue) grows linearly with depth.

en.text: The depth sweep reproduces the predicted degeneracy directly: averaged accuracy climbs for the first few levels and then declines as trees get deeper, for every setting of α. The timing panel makes the closed-form payoff concrete — because the TNTK does not recurse in depth, its cost is essentially flat, whereas the MLP-induced NTK grows linearly with depth. On the accuracy comparison, the MLP-induced kernel is stronger on average, but the tree kernel is not merely a curiosity: it wins outright on more than 30% of the individual datasets, exactly the cases where a tree's inductive bias is the better fit.

The split-hardness sweep quantifies the "sharper is better" story. The table below reports, for each α, the fraction of the 90 datasets on which the TNTK beats the MLP-induced NTK. The win rate climbs from 13.6% at the near-linear α = 0.5 to a peak of 34.9% at α = 32, and the whole hard-split range sits comfortably above the 11.8% managed by the RBF kernel.

en.caption: Table 1. TNTK win rate against the MLP-induced NTK across the 90 datasets, as a function of split hardness α (depth tuned from d = 1 to 29). The RBF kernel is shown for reference.

zh.text: 到底管不管用？90 个数据集上的核回归
有了理论，作者把 TNTK 当作一个实用的核来检验。他们在 90 个真实世界数据集上用 TNTK 做核回归，把深度从 d = 1 调到 29，并与无穷宽 MLP 诱导的核以及经典的 RBF 核作对比。

zh.caption: 图 6 左：90 个数据集上的平均准确率随树深度的变化（多条曲线对应不同分裂硬度 α），并以 MLP 诱导的 NTK 与 RBF 作参照；准确率随深度先升后降，正是核形状所预测的退化。右：核计算耗时，TNTK（橙）基本平坦，MLP 诱导 NTK（蓝）随深度线性增长。

zh.text: 深度扫描直接复现了预测的退化：对每一个 α，平均准确率都在最初几层上升，随后随着树变深而下降。耗时那一幅则把闭式的好处落到实处——由于 TNTK 不对深度递归，它的开销基本是平的，而 MLP 诱导的 NTK 则随深度线性增长。在准确率对比上，MLP 诱导的核平均更强，但树的核并不只是个摆设：它在超过 30% 的单个数据集上取胜，也就是那些树的归纳偏置更契合数据的场景。
分裂硬度的扫描量化了「越硬越好」这个故事。下表给出在每个 α 下，TNTK 在 90 个数据集中胜过 MLP 诱导 NTK 的比例。胜率从近线性的 α = 0.5 时的 13.6% 一路爬升，到 α = 32 时达到峰值 34.9%，而整个硬分裂区间都明显高于 RBF 核的 11.8%。

zh.caption: 表 1 在 90 个数据集上，TNTK 相对 MLP 诱导 NTK 的胜率，随分裂硬度 α 变化（深度从 d = 1 到 29 调优）。RBF 核作为参照。

有了理论，作者把 TNTK 当作一个实用的核来检验。他们在 90 个真实世界数据集上用 TNTK 做核回归，把深度从 d = 1 调到 29，并与无穷宽 MLP 诱导的核以及经典的 RBF 核作对比。

zh.caption: 图 6 左：90 个数据集上的平均准确率随树深度的变化（多条曲线对应不同分裂硬度 α），并以 MLP 诱导的 NTK 与 RBF 作参照；准确率随深度先升后降，正是核形状所预测的退化。右：核计算耗时，TNTK（橙）基本平坦，MLP 诱导 NTK（蓝）随深度线性增长。

zh.text: 深度扫描直接复现了预测的退化：对每一个 α，平均准确率都在最初几层上升，随后随着树变深而下降。耗时那一幅则把闭式的好处落到实处——由于 TNTK 不对深度递归，它的开销基本是平的，而 MLP 诱导的 NTK 则随深度线性增长。在准确率对比上，MLP 诱导的核平均更强，但树的核并不只是个摆设：它在超过 30% 的单个数据集上取胜，也就是那些树的归纳偏置更契合数据的场景。
分裂硬度的扫描量化了「越硬越好」这个故事。下表给出在每个 α 下，TNTK 在 90 个数据集中胜过 MLP 诱导 NTK 的比例。胜率从近线性的 α = 0.5 时的 13.6% 一路爬升，到 α = 32 时达到峰值 34.9%，而整个硬分裂区间都明显高于 RBF 核的 11.8%。

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 给无穷棵软树一把「核」尺子：Tree NTK 首次为软树集成提供理论解释
zh.subtitle: 日本国立情报学研究所 Kanoh 与 Sugiyama 推导出树的神经正切核（TNTK），一套理论同时解释了软树集成的全局收敛、参数共享为何免费、深树为何退化、以及分裂更硬为何更好。

en.text: On tabular data, gradient-boosted and neural decision trees remain the models to beat. One increasingly popular variant is the soft tree ensemble: instead of the hard, greedy splits of a classic decision tree, every splitting rule is made differentiable, so the whole forest can be trained end-to-end with gradient descent, exactly like a neural network. These models perform well, and practitioners have accumulated a toolbox of tricks to train them: sharing parameters across nodes, tuning how sharp the splits are, over-parameterizing the ensemble. What has been missing is theory. Almost nothing explained why soft tree ensembles train the way they do, when they generalize, or why those tricks work.

For neural networks, the tool that filled a similar gap was the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK). In the limit of infinitely many hidden units, a wide network trained by gradient descent behaves like kernel regression with a fixed, closed-form kernel, and that observation has explained training dynamics and generalization for the MLP, the CNN, and many other architectures. Each architecture induces its own distinct kernel. But no one had derived an NTK for tree models, so the soft-tree side of the tabular world stayed theoretically dark.

This paper, presented at ICLR 2022 by Ryuichi Kanoh and Mahito Sugiyama (National Institute of Informatics, NII, and SOKENDAI), closes that gap. It introduces the Tree Neural Tangent Kernel (TNTK): the kernel induced by an ensemble of infinitely many soft trees. From a single closed-form kernel, the authors derive global training convergence, prove that the parameter sharing used by oblivious-tree models costs nothing in this limit, show why very deep soft trees stop generalizing, and explain why sharper splits produce a more useful kernel.

en.caption: Figure 1. An ensemble of M soft trees. Each perfect binary tree routes an input through differentiable internal nodes (blue, with weight vectors w) down to leaf values (green, the response π). Every tree outputs a weighted sum over its leaves, and the ensemble averages the M tree outputs with a 1/√M scaling. The TNTK studies the limit M → ∞.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04983

zh.text: 在表格数据（tabular data）上，基于决策树的模型至今仍是最难被超越的一类。近年来一个受关注的变体是「软树集成（soft tree ensemble）」：它不像经典决策树那样在每个节点做硬性贪心划分，而是把每条分裂规则都改造成可微分形式，于是整片森林可以像神经网络一样用梯度下降端到端训练。这类模型在许多任务上表现很好，实践者也积累了一套训练技巧：节点间共享参数、调节分裂软硬、把集成过参数化。唯一缺的是理论——几乎没有工作能解释它们为何这样训练、何时能泛化，以及这些经验技巧为何有效。
对神经网络来说，填补类似空白的工具正是「神经正切核（Neural Tangent Kernel, NTK）」。在隐藏单元数趋于无穷的极限下，用梯度下降训练的宽网络等价于一个固定、有闭式表达的核所对应的核回归；这一观察解释了 MLP、CNN 等众多架构的训练动力学与泛化，而每种架构都会诱导出属于自己的核。但此前没有人为树模型推导出对应的 NTK，于是表格世界里软树这一侧一直处在理论的暗处。

这篇发表于 ICLR 2022 的论文，由日本国立情报学研究所（NII）与综合研究大学院大学（SOKENDAI）的 Ryuichi Kanoh 和 Mahito Sugiyama 完成，补上了这块拼图。他们提出「树的神经正切核（Tree Neural Tangent Kernel, TNTK）」，即由无穷多棵软树组成的集成所诱导的核。从这一个闭式核出发，作者推导出训练的全局收敛，证明 oblivious 树的参数共享在该极限下不损失表达力，并解释了深软树为何反而不再泛化、以及把分裂做硬为何更有用。

zh.caption: 图 1 由 M 棵软树组成的集成。每棵完全二叉树把输入沿可微分的内部节点（蓝色，带权向量 w）向下路由，直到叶子取值（绿色，即响应 π）。每棵树输出叶子上的加权和，集成再把 M 棵树的输出以 1/√M 的比例平均。TNTK 研究的是 M → ∞ 的极限。

en.caption: Figure 6. Left: averaged accuracy over 90 datasets versus tree depth, for a range of split-hardness values α, with the MLP-induced NTK and RBF baselines shown for reference. Accuracy first rises then falls with depth — exactly the degeneracy the kernel shape predicts. Right: kernel-computation time versus depth. The TNTK (orange) stays flat while the MLP-induced NTK (blue) grows linearly with depth.

en.text: From soft trees to a fixed kernel

A soft tree replaces each hard split with a smooth decision. At every internal node, instead of sending an input strictly left or right, the tree computes a probability of going each way using a scaled error function — essentially a smooth sigmoid whose steepness is set by a scaling parameter α. Small α gives a gentle, almost linear split; as α grows the split sharpens, and in the limit α → ∞ it recovers the hard split of an ordinary decision tree. Because every operation is differentiable, the internal weights and the leaf values can all be learned jointly by gradient descent.

The authors take an ensemble of M perfect binary soft trees of depth d, initialize the parameters randomly, and let M go to infinity. Their central result is that the ensemble's neural tangent kernel converges in probability to a deterministic kernel that no longer depends on the random initialization. The TNTK has a clean, interpretable structure: one contribution from the internal splitting nodes and one from the leaves, combined in closed form. Crucially, the split expectations have analytic expressions, so the whole kernel is available as a formula rather than a simulation. And because that formula is not a depth-by-depth recursion, computing the TNTK costs the same no matter how deep the trees are — a point that will matter later.

The formula folds together two ingredients evaluated on a pair of inputs: T, the probability that both inputs are routed the same way at a node, and its derivative in the input similarity. Written compactly, the depth-d kernel is 2^d · d · Σ · T^(d-1) · Ṫ  +  (2T)^d, where Σ is the inner product of the two inputs. The first term is the internal-node contribution, the second the leaf contribution; both are fixed once α and d are chosen.

zh.subtitle: 日本国立情报学研究所 Kanoh 与 Sugiyama 推导出树的神经正切核（TNTK），一套理论同时解释了软树集成的全局收敛、参数共享为何免费、深树为何退化、以及分裂更硬为何更好。

en.caption: Figure 1. An ensemble of M soft trees. Each perfect binary tree routes an input through differentiable internal nodes (blue, with weight vectors w) down to leaf values (green, the response π). Every tree outputs a weighted sum over its leaves, and the ensemble averages the M tree outputs with a 1/√M scaling. The TNTK studies the limit M → ∞.

en.text: Takeaways

The lasting contribution is conceptual: the NTK framework, previously a tool for neural networks, extends cleanly to tree ensembles. The resulting Tree NTK explains a range of soft-tree behavior from one theory — training converges globally, oblivious parameter sharing is free in the infinite limit, deep trees degenerate into a near-constant kernel, and sharper splits yield a more expressive one. Along the way it delivers a usable, depth-free kernel that is competitive with, and on more than 30% of datasets better than, the MLP-induced NTK, at a fraction of the computational cost as depth grows.

The honest boundaries are worth stating. The analysis lives in the infinite-ensemble limit and covers perfect binary trees; the empirical study is kernel regression on tabular datasets rather than large-scale deep learning, and on average the MLP-induced kernel still edges out the tree kernel. Even so, the TNTK gives soft tree ensembles something they lacked — a principled account of why they train and generalize as they do, and a concrete guide to the tricks that make them work.

zh.caption: 图 1 由 M 棵软树组成的集成。每棵完全二叉树把输入沿可微分的内部节点（蓝色，带权向量 w）向下路由，直到叶子取值（绿色，即响应 π）。每棵树输出叶子上的加权和，集成再把 M 棵树的输出以 1/√M 的比例平均。TNTK 研究的是 M → ∞ 的极限。

zh.text: 从软树到一个固定的核

软树把每个硬分裂替换成一次平滑的决策。在每个内部节点上，输入不再被严格地分到左边或右边，而是用一个「缩放误差函数（scaled error function）」计算向两侧走的概率——本质上是一个平滑的 sigmoid，其陡峭程度由缩放参数 α 控制。α 较小时分裂很温和、接近线性；α 增大时分裂变硬，而在 α → ∞ 的极限下就还原成普通决策树的硬分裂。由于每一步操作都可微分，内部权重和叶子取值都能用梯度下降联合学习。

作者取 M 棵深度为 d 的完全二叉软树组成集成，随机初始化参数，再让 M 趋于无穷。他们的核心结论是：该集成的神经正切核会依概率收敛到一个确定性的核，不再依赖随机初始化。TNTK 有一个清晰、可解释的结构：一部分来自内部分裂节点，一部分来自叶子，二者以闭式组合。关键在于，分裂的期望有解析表达式，所以整个核是一个公式而非一次模拟。又因为这个公式并不是对深度逐层递归的，计算 TNTK 的开销与树有多深无关——这一点在后面很重要。
这个公式把在一对输入上求值的两个量组合在一起：T，即两个输入在某节点被路由到同一侧的概率，以及它对输入相似度的导数。写得紧凑一些，深度为 d 的核是 2^d · d · Σ · T^(d-1) · Ṫ  +  (2T)^d，其中 Σ 是两个输入的内积。第一项是内部节点的贡献，第二项是叶子的贡献；一旦选定 α 与 d，二者都被固定下来。
